key_insight: Strongly coupled pentacene dimers can form a triplet-pair state with persistent singlet-like electronic mixing, and this mixing survives structural fluctuations over time.
engineering_relevance: For singlet-fission photovoltaics, this suggests that molecular planarity and strong coupling are key design levers for generating and retaining useful multiexcitonic states.
method: Polarization-controlled impulsive optical spectroscopy on a library of flexible pentacene dimers
Near-IR tracking of the (TT1)1-specific photoproduct feature
Anisotropy analysis supported by screened configuration-interaction electronic structure theory
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the triplet-pair signature forms only in planar conformations and that polarization anisotropy reveals persistent singlet-triplet mixing across diverse bridging motifs.
watch_item: The conclusions rely on a specific near-IR spectral marker and strongly coupled dimer systems, so transferability to less rigid or chemically different singlet-fission materials may be limited.
paper_title: Persistent singlet electronic character in the multiexcitonic triplet-pair state of strongly coupled pentacene singlet fission dimers
